title: Highlighted Note Reference

illustrates.quote: Retain font attributes unless all notes using the same reference mark are entirely emphasized. Do not retain font attributes for line numbers.

blocks.text: [ref:1]Predacious, fierce, secretive, majestic, and even wise are adjectives that describe the owl.
blocks.features: The word "Predacious" is highlighted (yellow background) rather than marked with a symbol; this highlighting is the reference mark per rule 16.3a.
Set off below a horizontal rule at the foot of the passage; "predacious" itself is bold.

print.surroundingText: Illustration directly below rule 16.7.3 (immediately following 16.6's gloss-note material), showing highlighting used as the print reference mark.
print.printFeatures: Boxed screenshot: one sentence with the word "Predacious" highlighted in yellow, a horizontal rule beneath the passage, then a glossary-style note below.

braille.notes: The highlighted word is preceded by a numeric reference indicator (@#1) rather than a repeat of the highlighting itself (braille has no highlight-emphasis equivalent, so a numbered reference mark is substituted, following the 'use the braille equivalent that represents that print symbol' principle even though print itself used emphasis, not a symbol, at this point). The note begins with the same numeral (^1) after the note separation line, then a second dashed rule ending in reference code #abc, then a lone '444' (ellipsis/continuation marker) on the final line.

uncertain: Whether '@#1' is the guide's own generic placeholder numeral (as opposed to a specific numbered-note braille sequence tied to this passage's context) was not independently confirmed beyond what the seven-line excerpt itself shows.
resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.5.1.f per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: line 12567 (the page-change dashed rule ending '#abc'), stripped of its 7-space left padding, is exactly 40 characters. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
